result.keywords: SummaryNetwork environments are becoming increasingly complex, making traffic monitoring and security analysis more difficult. To address unstable detection accuracy and the burden of centralized processing, this study proposes an adaptive traffic anomaly filtering framework for distributed intrusion detection systems. By combining support vector machine classification with edge computing, the method performs localized feature screening and model selection to reduce communication delay and improve response time. Experiments show that the approach can lower false alarms, support encrypted traffic recognition, and decrease workload on the central server while maintaining reliable classification performance.
result.title: Adaptive traffic anomaly filtering using edge-based support vector machines for distributed network monitoring.
